title: Curried Goat
subtitle: caribbean slow-braised goat curry
excerpt: Curried goat is a Caribbean classic of slow-braised goat shoulder in a fragrant curry spice blend with scotch bonnet and thyme until tender. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Curried goat arrived in Jamaica and Trinidad through the Indian indentured workers who came to the Caribbean in the nineteenth century. It is now one of the most beloved dishes across the region.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat gently from frozen or defrost overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the goat in the spices overnight for a deeper flavour.

glossaryTerms.definition: A spice blend of cumin, coriander, turmeric and others, widely used in Caribbean cooking from Indian influence.
Lean, slightly gamey meat that becomes tender with long, slow braising.

content.text: is lean and slightly gamey, and it responds beautifully to long, slow braising in spiced liquid. The
in this recipe is built from cumin, coriander and allspice. The spices go into the hot oil first, blooming briefly before the meat is added, which releases their aroma fully.

Goat shoulder is bone-in and fatty in parts. Those bones give the braising liquid more body and the fat melts in over the long cook. Ask your butcher to cut it into 5cm chunks. Two and a half hours is the minimum; three hours is better.
Heat the oil in the dutch oven over high heat. Brown the goat chunks in batches using tongs, turning to colour all sides, about 5 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 5 minutes. Add the cumin, coriander and allspice and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the goat to the pot. Pour in the stock and add the thyme and whole scotch bonnet. Bring to a simmer.
Cover tightly and cook over very low heat for 2 hours. Add the potato chunks and cook for a further 30 minutes until the goat is completely tender and the potato is cooked through.
Remove the scotch bonnet and thyme. Season to taste. Serve with rice and peas or roti.

attrs.problem: The goat is still tough after 2.5 hours.
attrs.solution: Goat can vary greatly in age. Older animals take longer. Add more stock if needed and continue cooking in 30-minute increments.
Toast the spices in the dry pan for 30 seconds before adding the onion. Dry-toasting wakes up older ground spices.
They were added too early or the simmer was too vigorous. Add potatoes only in the last 30 minutes and keep the heat as low as possible.

content.text: Curried goat is a celebration dish across Jamaica, Trinidad and Guyana. It is the centrepiece of weddings and christenings. In the UK it is found at Caribbean restaurants and the Notting Hill Carnival, often served in a roti wrap. The dish reflects the meeting of Indian and Caribbean culinary traditions.
